body.statement: For every finite \(X\), fixed \(\ell\), finite \(\mathcal I\ni\varnothing\), and loopless graph pair \(G,H\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\). Consequently, \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)=\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if both \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\) and \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(H,G)\) hold. This criterion is exact on lower-dimensional rank, cancellation, nullification, invisible-source, and source-symmetry strata, and it is a finite graph-generated compatibility representation rather than the original structural-existence formula.
body.proof_tex:
We first prove directed containment.  Assume
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H),          \tag{12}
\]
and fix \(C\in\mathcal D_G\).  The already established Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-mixing-realization}\) supplies an exact-support \(G\)-matrix \(Q\) satisfying every required principal invertibility condition and having \((Q^{-1})_{X,:}=C\).  Put on this matrix the diagnostic independent finite-support source vector supplied by Lemma \(\texttt{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\).  Its coordinates are nonconstant and non-Gaussian, so Definition \(\texttt{def:exact-support-model-class}\) makes this an admissible mechanism; no centering or moment condition is required.

By (12), the resulting entire response-kernel tuple is generated by an admissible \(H\)-mechanism.  Let \(D\) be its observed mixing matrix.  The backward implication of exact mixing realization gives \(D\in\mathcal D_H\).  Equality of the observational components is
\[
 \mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=\mathcal L(D\eta).
\]
Diagnostic rigidity therefore supplies a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero \(a_i\) such that
\[
 C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)},\qquad i\in U_C.                              \tag{13}
\]

Fix \(S\in\mathcal I\).  By Lemma \(\texttt{lem:intervention-pushforward}\), equality of the two kernels says
\[
 \mathcal L\bigl(R_S(C)\varepsilon+T_S(C)x\bigr)
 =\mathcal L\bigl(R_S(D)\eta+T_S(D)x\bigr)
 \quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^S.                              \tag{14}
\]
At \(x=0\), the residual laws in (14) equal a common probability measure \(\mu_S\).  Thus for every \(x\), translation of \(\mu_S\) by \(T_S(C)x\) equals translation by \(T_S(D)x\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:probability-translation-rigidity}\) gives
\[
 (T_S(C)-T_S(D))x=0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^S,
\]
and hence \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\).  This also covers an empty domain or codomain.  We have verified every clause of \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\).

Conversely, assume \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\), and take an arbitrary admissible \(G\)-mechanism with observed mixing matrix \(C\) and independent nonconstant non-Gaussian source vector \(\varepsilon\).  Exact mixing realization places \(C\) in \(\mathcal D_G\).  Choose a cover witness \((D,f,a)\).  The same theorem constructs an exact-support, regime-solvable \(H\)-matrix with observed mixing \(D\).  For \(j\in U_D\), define once and for all
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\varepsilon_i.                              \tag{15}
\]
Disjoint, nonempty fibers make these variables mutually independent.  The support argument and L\'evy--Cram\'er argument in the proof of Lemma \(\texttt{lem:finite-mixture-containment-unrestricted}\) show that each is nonconstant and non-Gaussian.  Choose arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources on the invisible columns, independent of (15).  Thus this is one admissible \(H\)-source tuple, common to all regimes.  Equation (13), now as a cover clause, gives the samplewise equality \(C\varepsilon=D\eta\).

For every \(S\in\mathcal I\) and \(i\in U_C\), proportionality of the full observed columns and equality of response matrices imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_S(C)_{:,i}
 &=C_{X\setminus S,i}-T_S(C)C_{S,i}\\
 &=a_i\bigl(D_{X\setminus S,f(i)}-T_S(D)D_{S,f(i)}\bigr)\\
 &=a_iR_S(D)_{:,f(i)}.                                                 \tag{16}
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(i\notin U_C\), its residual column is zero by the intervention-pushforward lemma; surjectivity ensures that every visible \(D\)-column appears in (15).  Summing (16) over the source fibers yields
\[
 R_S(C)\varepsilon=R_S(D)\eta.
\]
Together with \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\), the pushforward identity proves equality of the two kernels for every \(x\), simultaneously for every \(S\).  Hence the whole tuple belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\), proving the reverse implication.

We have established
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H).
\]
Applying this equivalence in both directions proves the equality criterion.  Every zero pattern, rank incidence, and punctured exact-support condition is retained in \(\mathcal D_G\) and \(\mathcal D_H\); no generic, closure, boundary, or limiting argument occurs.
body.justification: This is the exact-support theorem-level kernel: it proves that the finite coupled cover is sound and complete for joint response-kernel containment and equality under one shared mechanism.
body.gap: Dai et al. characterize the observational zero-allowed class, while existing latent intervention results do not characterize cyclic full-law response-kernel equality with shared source laws across all regimes.
body.consumer: Perturbational feedback analyses can enumerate every exact-support hidden-variable graph compatible with the full population intervention tuple instead of treating one fitted graph as uniquely identified.
